proposals.evidence: Turner 9190 bahutva explicitly lists European Romani but/būt 'much, many'. The source prints Zargari but 'many; much; several' under quantitative pronouns (p. 137 §3.3.7.1) and but 'very' under degree adverbs (p. 143 §3.20.1.5). The latter is a source-documented intensifier use of the same inherited quantity word; its gloss is preserved separately. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

proposals.evidence: Turner 11589 vā́śyatē explicitly gives European Romani baš- 'to bark, crow' and, in the same parenthesis, German Romani bašno 'cock'. The source prints Zargari bāśno 'cock' among masculine nouns (p. 132 §3.1.9). The -no bird noun is a documented Romani derivative within this family, not a claimed independent Sanskrit noun. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.
